scenarios.name: empty_query
scenarios.description: An empty DiscoveryQuery (no predicates specified) must match all instances in the repository.

scenarios.name: tier_filter_note
scenarios.description: A tier:0 filter returns only Note instances (Tier 0). Tier 2 instances must not appear.

scenarios.name: tier_filter_record
scenarios.description: A tier:2 filter returns only Record instances (Tier 2). Tier 0 instances must not appear.

scenarios.name: type_name_article
scenarios.description: A typeName:'article' filter returns exactly all Records whose typeNamespace-qualified type name is 'article'. Tier 0 instances and Records of other types must not appear.

scenarios.name: type_namespace
scenarios.description: A typeNamespace:'com.example.discovery' filter returns all Tier 2 Records in that namespace. Tier 0 instances have no typeNamespace and must not appear.

scenarios.name: type_id_project
scenarios.description: A typeId filter matching the 'project' type UUID returns exactly the two project Records.

scenarios.name: container_alpha
scenarios.description: A containerId filter for container-alpha returns only the three articles registered as members via memberInstanceIds. Instances not in that container must not appear.

scenarios.name: container_beta
scenarios.description: A containerId filter for container-beta returns only the two project Records registered as members via memberInstanceIds.

scenarios.name: single_tag_searchable
scenarios.description: A tag filter for ['searchable'] returns all instances carrying that tag string. Instances without the tag must not appear.

scenarios.name: multi_tag_and
scenarios.description: A tag filter for ['searchable', 'indexed'] uses AND semantics: only instances carrying BOTH tags must be returned. Instances carrying only one of the two tags must not appear.

scenarios.name: lifecycle_published
scenarios.description: A lifecycleState:'published' filter returns only Records in that lifecycle state. Records in other states and Tier 0 instances (which have no lifecycleState) must not appear.

scenarios.name: lifecycle_draft
scenarios.description: A lifecycleState:'draft' filter returns only Records in the draft state.

scenarios.name: type_and_lifecycle_combined
scenarios.description: Combined typeName and lifecycleState predicates are evaluated as an AND conjunction. Only Records satisfying both must be returned.

scenarios.name: content_match_discovery
scenarios.description: A contentMatch:'discovery' predicate must include every instance whose Text Projection contains a segment whose normalized text contains 'discovery' as a substring. The guaranteed-recall floor is articles 1, 2, and 4 (title/body contain 'discovery') and project-2 (description contains 'discovery'). Implementations may return additional instances.

scenarios.name: content_match_indexing
scenarios.description: A contentMatch:'indexing' predicate must include every instance with a Text Projection segment containing 'indexing'. Articles 1 and 3 each have 'indexing' as a multiselect topics value. This tests that multiselect elements each contribute a separate segment.

scenarios.name: content_match_indexed_tag_and_label
scenarios.description: A contentMatch:'indexed' predicate must include instances where 'indexed' appears in tag segments (articles 1, 3 and project-1) and in the string label field of metric-1 ('Indexed Record Count'). This tests that both tag segments and string field segments are projected.

scenarios.name: content_match_combined_type_and_content
scenarios.description: Combined typeName and contentMatch predicates: must return only article instances (structured filter, exact) that also match the content floor for 'draft' (the select field value 'draft' is searchable). The floor is articles 2 and 5 (both have status field value 'draft').

scenarios.name: i120_include_format_markdown
scenarios.description: I-120: datatype string with format markdown is searchable. Recall floor — the article carrying it must be found.

scenarios.name: i120_include_list_element_first
scenarios.description: I-120: a list-cardinality string emits one segment per array element. Element 0 must be independently recallable.

scenarios.name: i120_include_list_element_middle
scenarios.description: I-120: element 1 of the same open list. Asserted separately from element 0 so a projection that concatenates the list into a single segment still passes only if every element is recallable.

scenarios.name: i120_include_list_element_last
scenarios.description: I-120: element 2 of the same open list. See the README note on what this trio does NOT assert (segment count and order are not observable through DiscoveryHit).

scenarios.name: i120_list_segments_order
scenarios.description: srs#483/#317-F2: expectedSegments asserts segment COUNT and ORDER directly, closing the gap the i120_include_list_element_* trio leaves open (each of those only proves independent recallability). Same field as that trio: article-1's open list-cardinality 'aliases', which I-120 requires to emit one segment per array element in array order.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_format_uuid
scenarios.description: I-120: format uuid contributes no segment. The token is the uuid's own leading group and appears nowhere else in the fixture, so any hit means the excluded Field was projected. Asserted against the allow-list (CC-25), not as a format!=uri test.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_format_email
scenarios.description: I-120: format email contributes no segment. Same allow-list reasoning as the uuid case.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_integer
scenarios.description: I-120: datatype integer contributes no segment. Distinct from the legacy `number` exclusion — the erratum added integer as its own datatype.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_date_time
scenarios.description: I-120: datatype date-time contributes no segment. Distinct from `date`; the erratum made date-time a first-class datatype rather than a string format.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_map_value
scenarios.description: I-120: datatype map contributes no segment. The probe is a map VALUE, the likelier of the two to be projected by an implementation that walks the carrier generically.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_map_key
scenarios.description: I-120: a map's KEYS are not segments either. Asserted separately from the value: a projection that emitted keys but not values would pass the value case alone.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_ref_reference
scenarios.description: I-120: datatype ref in mode reference contributes no segment. The probe is the referenced project's own instance id — a hit would mean opaque identifiers are searchable as prose. project-1 is NOT expected: a content match is over Text Projection segments, and no segment contains this id.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_ref_inline
scenarios.description: I-120 + CC-27: datatype ref in mode inline contributes no segment either, knowingly. The token sits in the nested composite's `display_name`, a plain string Field that WOULD be searchable at the top level. Recursive composite Text Projection is undefined — this fixture asserts exclusion only, and the unfindability is a recorded accepted cost.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_dependent
scenarios.description: I-120: datatype dependent contributes no segment. Excluded by its own datatype — the projection does not resolve `dependsOn` (here, the searchable `title`) before deciding.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_number
scenarios.description: I-120: datatype number contributes no segment. Probes `legacy_score`, whose value appears in no projectable string anywhere in the fixture — `word_count`'s values (42, 28, 150, 75, 99) are all too short to probe meaningfully.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_boolean
scenarios.description: I-120: datatype boolean contributes no segment. No projectable string in the fixture contains "true" or "false", so a hit means a boolean was rendered into a segment — `is_published` is true on two articles and `is_active` on one metric. Assumes the rendering would be the JSON literal, which is the only plausible one; a projection emitting "1"/"yes" would evade this and no assertion can cover every rendering of a value with no text.

scenarios.name: i120_exclude_date
scenarios.description: I-120: datatype date contributes no segment. "2025-01-01" occurs exactly once in the fixture — as article-4's `publish_date`, the excluded Field itself — so any hit means the date was projected. Distinct from `date-time` (i120_exclude_date_time), which the Rev-7 erratum made a separate datatype.

scenarios.name: ff_in_string_single
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R3]: in on a closed string selects records whose value equals a listed value. Articles 1 and 3 are published; the new article has no status and is not selected.

scenarios.name: ff_in_string_multi
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R3]: in is OR over its listed values. Draft (2, 5) or archived (4).

scenarios.name: ff_notin_string
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R3]: notIn selects records that have a value and it is not listed. The new article has no status, so it is NOT returned (notIn is not the complement of in).

scenarios.name: ff_notin_all_values_empty
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R3]/[R5]: every article with a status holds one of the three listed values, and the article with no status never satisfies notIn, so the result is empty.

scenarios.name: ff_in_list_string
scenarios.description: RFC-056 Change B: on a list-valued string, in holds when any element is listed. Articles 1 and 3 list indexing.

scenarios.name: ff_in_list_any_element
scenarios.description: RFC-056 Change B: in holds when any element is listed, whichever one. Article 1 has search, article 4 has legacy.

scenarios.name: ff_notin_list_string
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R3]: notIn on a list holds when the list is non-empty and no element is listed. Article 6 (empty list) is not returned.

scenarios.name: ff_notin_list_any_listed_element_excludes
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R3]: one listed element anywhere in the list excludes the record. Article 1 (search), 2 (text) and 4 (legacy) each hold a listed element; 3 (performance, indexing) and 5 (metadata) hold none.

scenarios.name: ff_empty_list_in_all_values
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R5]: an empty list is no value, so it satisfies no in. Listing every topic selects articles 1-5, never the new article whose topics is [].

scenarios.name: ff_empty_list_missing_true
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R5]: an empty list is no value, so missing:true holds. Only the new article has no topics.

scenarios.name: ff_in_integer
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R3]: in on an integer compares by numeric value. Only article 4 holds 4.

scenarios.name: ff_in_integer_written_with_decimal_point
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R3]: 12 equals a stored 12.0. Article 5 stores 12.0.

scenarios.name: ff_in_integer_large
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R3]: exact decimal comparison for a large integer. Article 1 holds 987654321.

scenarios.name: ff_in_boolean_true
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R3]: in on a boolean. Articles 1 and 3 are published (is_published true); the metric Type has no is_published.

scenarios.name: ff_in_boolean_false
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R3]: in [false] selects stored false only. The new article stores no is_published and is not selected.

scenarios.name: ff_notin_boolean
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R3]: notIn [true] selects records that hold false, not records with no value.

scenarios.name: ff_vocab_alias_listed
scenarios.description: RFC-056 Change B: a listed alias resolves to its term key. short-form is an alias of brief; article 2 stores brief and article 3 stores the alias, and both are selected.

scenarios.name: ff_vocab_key_listed
scenarios.description: RFC-056 Change B: the listed key brief selects the same records, both the key stored by article 2 and the alias stored by article 3.

scenarios.name: ff_vocab_notin_alias
scenarios.description: RFC-056 Change B: notIn resolves aliases too. Listing the alias short-form excludes briefs; article 1 (feature) remains. Articles with no section are not returned.

scenarios.name: ff_vocab_in_two_terms
scenarios.description: RFC-056 Change B: in over a key and an alias of different terms. feature (article 1) or short-form, resolved to brief (articles 2, 3).

scenarios.name: ff_range_date_day_bounds
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R4]: day bounds, both included. 2026-06-01 (article 1) through 2026-06-26 (article 5) are both selected; 2026-05-15 is before and 2025-01-01 earlier still.

scenarios.name: ff_range_date_month_bounds
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R4]: a month bound covers the whole month. June 2026 holds 2026-06-01 (article 1) and 2026-06-26 (article 5).

scenarios.name: ff_range_date_year_2026
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R4]: a year bound covers the whole year. 2026 holds articles 1, 3 and 5.

scenarios.name: ff_range_date_year_2025
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R4]: a year bound covers the whole year. 2025 holds only article 4 (2025-01-01).

scenarios.name: ff_range_date_open_forward
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R4]: a range with only from is open-ended forward. On or after 2026-06-02 leaves article 5 (2026-06-26); article 1 (2026-06-01) is before the bound.

scenarios.name: ff_range_date_open_backward_month
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R4]: a range with only to is open-ended backward, and a month to-bound ends at the month end. On or before 31 May 2026 holds article 3 (2026-05-15) and article 4 (2025-01-01).

scenarios.name: ff_range_date_from_after_to
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R4]: a range whose from lies after its to is valid and selects nothing.

scenarios.name: ff_range_list_dates_any_element
scenarios.description: RFC-056 Change B: range on a list holds when any element falls within the bounds. Article 1 has 2026-09-20 in September 2026.

scenarios.name: ff_range_list_dates_between_elements
scenarios.description: RFC-056 Change B: a range lying between the elements selects nothing. Article 1 holds 2026-03-10 and 2026-09-20, neither within April to August 2026.

scenarios.name: ff_range_list_dates_open_backward
scenarios.description: RFC-056 Change B: open-ended range on a list. Only article 2 has an element (2025-12-01) on or before the end of 2025.

scenarios.name: ff_range_number_inclusive
scenarios.description: RFC-056 Change B: both bounds included. word_count 40 to 80 selects 42 (article 1) and 75 (article 4).

scenarios.name: ff_range_number_bound_equals_value
scenarios.description: RFC-056 Change B: a bound equal to a stored value includes it. word_count from 75 selects 75 (article 4), 99 (article 5) and 150 (article 3).

scenarios.name: ff_range_number_decimal_bound
scenarios.description: RFC-056 Change B: a decimal bound is compared as given. 41.5 to 42 selects 42 (article 1) only.

scenarios.name: ff_range_number_open_backward
scenarios.description: RFC-056 Change B: only to is open-ended backward, and the bound is included. word_count to 28 selects article 2 (28).

scenarios.name: ff_range_number_from_after_to
scenarios.description: RFC-056 Change B: a numeric range whose from exceeds its to selects nothing.

scenarios.name: ff_range_integer_fractional_bound
scenarios.description: RFC-056 Change B: an integer Field accepts a fractional bound, compared as given. 3.5 to 12 selects 4 (article 4) and 12.0 (article 5), and not 987654321 (article 1).

scenarios.name: ff_range_integer_open_forward
scenarios.description: RFC-056 Change B: open-ended integer range. From 12.5 selects only 987654321 (article 1); 12.0 is below the bound.

scenarios.name: ff_missing_true
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R5]: missing:true selects articles with no publish_date: article 2 and the new article. Other Types and Notes are never returned.

scenarios.name: ff_missing_false
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R5]: missing:false selects articles that hold a publish_date (1, 3, 4, 5).

scenarios.name: ff_missing_true_no_status
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R5]: only the new article lacks a status.

scenarios.name: ff_missing_false_integer
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R5]: missing:false on read_minutes selects the three articles that hold one (1, 4, 5), including the one written 12.0.

scenarios.name: ff_missing_true_boolean_owning_type_only
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R6]: is_published belongs to article. missing:true selects the new article only; the metric, projects and the note, whose Types lack the Field, are not returned.

scenarios.name: ff_field_outside_type_selects_nothing
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R6]: is_active belongs to metric, not article. With typeName article no record can satisfy the filter.

scenarios.name: ff_field_outside_type_missing_true
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R6]: missing:true on a metric Field returns no article, project or Note. The only metric record holds is_active, so the result is empty.

scenarios.name: ff_field_in_own_type_control
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R6]: control for the two scenarios above. is_active in [true] selects the metric record, whose Type contains the Field.

scenarios.name: ff_project_field_outside_article
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R6]: priority belongs to project. With typeName article nothing is selected, though project-1 holds high.

scenarios.name: ff_project_field_own_type_control
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R6]: control. priority in [high] selects project-1 only; articles lack the Field.

scenarios.name: ff_unknown_field_id_in
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R6]: a fieldId that names no installed Field selects no instances (the implementation also warns, which a set cannot express).

scenarios.name: ff_unknown_field_id_missing_true
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R6]: an unresolved fieldId selects nothing even for missing:true; no record counts as lacking a Field that does not exist.

scenarios.name: ff_with_type_name_and_tag
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R1]: field filters conjoin with typeName and tag. Articles tagged searchable are 1 and 2; word_count from 30 leaves article 1 (42), dropping article 2 (28).

scenarios.name: ff_with_tag_and_in
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R1]: tag indexed carries articles 1 and 3 and project-1; status in [published] keeps articles 1 and 3 only, since a project lacks the Field.

scenarios.name: ff_with_container
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R1]: container-alpha holds articles 1, 2 and 3; publish_date in 2026 leaves 1 and 3 (article 2 has none).

scenarios.name: ff_two_filters_conjunction
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R1]: every filter must hold. status published (1, 3) and publish_date from 2026-06 (1, 5) leaves article 1.

scenarios.name: ff_empty_filter_list_no_effect
scenarios.description: RFC-056 [R1]: an empty fieldFilters list does not change the selection. typeName project selects both projects.
